title: CodeChallenge: Evolution of Alice and Edgar (part 2)

cues.en: This video is the grand finale of the code challenge that we started developing in the previous video,
cues.zh: 這支影片是上一支開始的程式挑戰大結局，

cues.en: so you definitely need to have gone through the previous video to start working on this one.
cues.zh: 所以一定要先完成上一支，再開始這裡。

cues.en: You are going to train the Alice and Edgar models on their respective texts, as you have done previously.
cues.zh: 你會像之前一樣，分別用各自文本訓練愛麗絲與愛倫坡模型。

cues.en: In this section, you can use 121 training samples and a learning rate of ten to the minus five.
cues.zh: 這部分可用 121 次訓練抽樣，學習率 10 的負 5 次方。

cues.en: So this is a very gentle fine tuning.
cues.zh: 所以是非常輕微的微調。

cues.en: We do not want to train too fast and we do not want to overfit on these texts.
cues.zh: 不希望訓練太快，也不想對這些文本過度擬合。

cues.en: Every ten samples you can calculate the Bert classification and write out a report.
cues.zh: 每十次抽樣，可以計算 BERT 分類結果，印出報告。

cues.en: It will look something like this.
cues.zh: 看起來會像這樣。

cues.en: So here we print out the losses for the Alice and the Edgar model.
cues.zh: 這裡印出愛麗絲與愛倫坡模型的損失。

cues.en: And here is the accuracy of the Bert classification.
cues.zh: 這是 BERT 分類的準確率。

cues.en: Vacation.
cues.zh: 也就是分類準確率。

cues.en: Of course, the accuracy starts off at around 50%, and the question is what happens as we progress through learning?
cues.zh: 當然，一開始約 50%，問題是隨著學習推進，會如何變化？

cues.en: Now, in theory, you could evaluate the Bert classification accuracy on each of 121 training samples.
cues.zh: 理論上，可以在全部 121 次訓練抽樣中，每次都評估 BERT 分類準確率。

cues.en: The problem is that generating a batch of data and having Bert do the classification takes quite a while.
cues.zh: 但產生一批資料，再讓 BERT 分類，需要不少時間。

cues.en: So if you evaluate more often, then the whole training loop just starts to take a really long time.
cues.zh: 評估越頻繁，整個訓練迴圈就會越慢。

cues.en: On the other hand, with the parameters that I set up, this whole training loop takes in my hands with

cues.en: I guess it depends on how patient you are.
cues.zh: 我想就看你有多少耐心。

cues.en: So therefore, using a classifier, uh, is a interesting alternative approach to quantifying the performance
cues.zh: 所以，使用分類器是另一種有趣的方法，量化評估

cues.en: So the idea is that if the Bert classifier model can predict with 90% accuracy which style is being
cues.zh: 概念是，如果 BERT 分類器能以 90% 準確率，預測

cues.en: generated by these two models here, then we can consider that this training is a success regardless of what the loss looks like.
cues.zh: 兩個模型生成的風格，就能認為訓練成功，不管損失看起來如何。

cues.en: Now remember that this classifier was trained on the actual text.
cues.zh: 記住，分類器訓練使用的是實際文本，

cues.en: So the actual books from Through the Looking Glass and Edgar Allan Poe's poems.
cues.zh: 也就是《鏡中奇緣》與愛倫坡詩集。

cues.en: The data that it's actually classifying does not come from those texts.
cues.zh: 但實際分類的資料，不是直接來自那些文本，

cues.en: It is generated by these two models.
cues.zh: 而是這兩個模型生成的。

cues.en: And these two models were trained on those two books.
cues.zh: 這兩個模型又是用那兩本書訓練的。

cues.en: So there's nothing circular or inherently biased about this, uh, assessment, this quantification of the performance of these two models.
cues.zh: 因此，這個評估、這種量化兩模型表現的方式，沒有循環論證或內在偏差。

cues.en: It's actually a really nice setup.
cues.zh: 這其實是很好的設計。

cues.en: It's a nice way to evaluate generative models.
cues.zh: 是評估生成模型的好方法。

cues.en: Well, that was quite a whirlwind of a code challenge.
cues.zh: 這個程式挑戰真是內容密集。

cues.en: I hope you feel like your brain expanded a little bit from these exercises, and from this entire section.
cues.zh: 希望這些練習，以及整個章節，讓你的腦袋又擴充了一些。

cues.en: I have mentioned earlier that evaluating generative models is really difficult.
cues.zh: 前面提過，評估生成模型很困難。

cues.en: It sounds very nice to use a third model to quantify the generative performance of two other models.
cues.zh: 用第三個模型來量化另外兩個的生成表現，聽起來很好。

cues.en: And in general, that is a promising avenue of research and application.
cues.zh: 整體而言，這確實是有前景的研究與應用方向。

cues.en: But the problem is that such an approach can also give a false sense of confidence when it doesn't work perfectly.
cues.zh: 但問題是，當這種方法不是完美運作時，也可能帶來虛假的信心。

cues.en: One clear example of this is language models that are designed to detect whether, for example, a report
cues.zh: 一個明顯例子，是用語言模型判斷，像學生

cues.en: that a student submits for a grade was written by a human or by an AI.
cues.zh: 交來評分的報告，究竟是人寫的，還是 AI 寫的。

cues.en: You've probably come across discussions like this online.
cues.zh: 你可能在網路看過這類討論。

cues.en: But basically these AI detectors just don't work very well.
cues.zh: 但基本上，這些 AI 偵測器效果不太好。

cues.en: They will label AI written text as human and human written text as AI.
cues.zh: 會把 AI 文字標成人類，也把人類文字標成 AI。

cues.en: So having a text classification model, it can be a great solution for some kinds of problems, but it is not universally a solution.
cues.zh: 所以，文字分類模型能解決某些問題，但並不是通用解方。
